Sports Network|TSN]] |via=[[YouTube]] }} born June 19, 2002) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]], where he was named a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-America]] and [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] after his sophomore season. Mathurin was selected sixth overall by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. He was voted to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] in [[2022–23 NBA season|2023]] and finished fourth in voting for the 2023 [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] award.{{cite web |title=2022-23 Kia NBA All-Rookie teams |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-23-all-rookie-teams-announced}} ==Early life and career== Mathurin was born and raised in [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]].{{cite web | last=Dopirak | first=Dustin | title=Pacers: Meet the Bennedict Mathurin you don't see on the court | website=IndyStar | date=2023-03-22 | url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2023/03/22/pacers-meet-the-bennedict-mathurin-you-dont-see-on-the-court/69934253007/ | access-date=2025-05-30}} He grew up playing [[ice hockey]] and [[Canadian football]] as a [[quarterback]].{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=With late brother as both memory and motivation, Arizona Wildcats commit Bennedict Mathurin charts course for basketball future |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/with-late-brother-as-both-memory-and-motivation-arizona-wildcats-commit-bennedict-mathurin-charts-course/article_4c38dbe1-5451-5ce8-a465-1555ca04ec4f.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=April 26, 2020}} He competed for the Quebec provincial basketball team.{{cite magazine |last=Rose |first=Aaron |title=Mathurin, Prosper pioneers at NBA Academy |url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/canada-basketball/bennedict-mathurin-olivier-prosper-pioneers-at-nba-academy |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=April 29, 2020}} In 2018, Mathurin joined the [[NBA Academy]] Latin America in [[Mexico City]], becoming its first Canadian-born player.{{cite web |last=Holmes |first=C. J. |title=The evolution of Ben Mathurin, and an inside look at the NBA academies |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1767862/2020/05/04/the-evolution-of-ben-mathurin-and-an-inside-look-at-the-nba-academies/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=May 3, 2020}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], choosing the Wildcats over [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]].{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Arizona Wildcats basketball lands commitment from Ben Mathurin |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2020/01/16/arizona-wildcats-basketball-lands-commitment-ben-mathurin/4487497002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=January 16, 2020}} He was considered the best Canadian prospect in his class by North Pole Hoops.{{cite web |last=Sbiet |first=Elias |title=Bennedict Mathurin Commits to Arizona, Canadian NBA Prospect For The Wildcats |url=https://northpolehoops.com/2020/01/16/bennedict-mathurin-commits-to-arizona-canadian-nba-prospect-for-the-wildcats/ |website=North Pole Hoops |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=January 16, 2020}} ==College career== On January 2, 2021, Mathurin posted 24 points and 11 rebounds in an 86–82 win over [[2020–21 Washington State Cougars men's basketball team|Washington State]].{{cite web |last=Kelapire |first=Ryan |title=Freshman Bennedict Mathurin quickly becoming a star at Arizona |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2021/1/15/22232338/bennedict-mathurin-star-arizona-wildcats-basketball-nba-draft-freshman-oregon-state-wahsington |website=Arizona Desert Swarm |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=January 15, 2021}} On January 14, he recorded 31 points and eight rebounds in a 98–64 win over [[2020–21 Oregon State Beavers men's basketball team|Oregon State]].{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Arizona's Bennedict Mathurin is developing into a 'special player,' and more attention is coming |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/arizonas-bennedict-mathurin-is-developing-into-a-special-player-and-more-attention-is-coming/article_7989d03e-cff8-5201-81f3-5818e62dc087.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=January 16, 2021}} Mathurin averaged 10.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game, shooting 41.8 percent from three-point range. Despite gaining interest as a draft prospect, he decided to return for his sophomore season.{{cite web |last=Pedersen |first=Brian |title=Arizona wing Bennedict Mathurin to return for sophomore season |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2021/4/23/22400507/arizona-wildcats-bennedict-mathurin-nba-draft-return-sophomore-tommy-lloyd-2021-wing |website=Arizona Desert Swarm |access-date=April 26, 2021 |date=April 23, 2021}} On December 11, 2021, Mathurin scored 30 points in a 83–79 win against [[2021–22 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]].{{cite news |title=Wildcats G Bennedict Mathurin drops 30 points in Arizona's win at Illinois |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2932098/wildcats-bennedict-mathurin-drops-30-points-in-arizona-win-at-illinois/ |access-date=January 28, 2022 |work=Arizona Sports |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 11, 2021}} Mathurin won the 2022 [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 Tournament Most Outstanding Player]] after leading the Wildcats to their eighth conference tournament title. He was named [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]], the ninth player in Arizona Wildcats history to do so.{{cite press release|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance.aspx|title=2021-22 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva|publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |access-date=March 8, 2022}} Following his Sophomore season, Mathurin was voted a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-America]], the fifth in Wildcat history to make second team and thirtieth All-American in school history.{{Cite web |title=2022-23 Arizona Wildcat Basketball Media Guide |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/documents/2022/11/9/PRINT-MBB_2023_Guide_UpdatedFeb.pdf}} By winning conference player of the year he became the 31st Arizona Wildcat men's basketball player to have his name put into the school's Ring of Honor.{{Cite web |title=Arizona Men's Basketball Ring of Honor Inductees |date=17 January 2023 |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2023/1/17/mens-basketball-mccray-ring-of-honor-ceremony-scheduled-for-jan-21.aspx}} On April 14, 2022, Mathurin declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=2022-04-14 |title=Projected lottery pick Bennedict Mathurin declares for NBA draft |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/04/14/arizona-bennedict-mathurin-nba-draft/ |access-date=2022-06-19 |website=The Rookie Wire|publisher=USA Today}}{{Cite web |date=2022-04-14 |access-date=2022-06-19 |website=The Athletic}} == Professional career == === Indiana Pacers (2022–2026) === ====2022–23 season: All–Rookie First Team honors==== Mathurin was selected with the 6th overall pick by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. He is the first ever player from [[Montreal]] to be selected as a lottery pick. He joined the seventh overall pick, [[Shaedon Sharpe]], as the only Canadians drafted in the first round that year. Mathurin was the Pacers' highest pick the franchise has owned since selecting [[Rik Smits]] second overall in the [[1988 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |last=East |first=Tony |date=2022-07-03 |title=Indiana Pacers Facing Their Most Important NBA draft in Decades |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tonyeast/2022/06/22/indiana-pacers-facing-their-most-important-nba-draft-in-decades |access-date=2022-07-03 |website=Forbes.com}} On July 3, 2022, Mathurin signed his rookie contract with the Pacers.{{Cite web |last=Grand |first=Kyle |date=2022-07-03 |title=Pacers sign Bennedict Mathurin |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-bennedict-mathurin |access-date=2022-07-03 |website=NBA.com}} On July 8, he made his [[NBA Summer League]] debut, recording 23 points and four rebounds in a 96–84 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |date=2022-07-08 |title=Hot Takes on Pacers' Bennedict Mathurin in 1st Game Since Calling out LeBron |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10041441-hot-takes-on-pacers-bennedict-mathurin-in-1st-game-since-calling-out-lebron-james |access-date=2022-07-08 |website=bleacherreport.com}} Ten days rookie Bennedict Mathurin named to NBA All-Summer League Second Team Indianapolis Star}} On October 19, Mathurin made his regular season debut coming off the bench, recording 19 points in a 114–107 loss to the [[2022–23 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.indycornrows.com/2022/10/19/23413866/tyrese-haliburton-and-bennedict-mathurin-shine-despite-indinaa-pacers-loss-to-washington-wizards|title=Tyrese Haliburton and The rookie is averaging 24 points on 11-21 from 3 |access-date=October 26, 2022}} On October 26, he became the first Pacer to score 100–plus points through their first five career games.{{cite tweet |user=theathleticnba |number=1585483683749937156 |date=October 27, 2022 |title=Bennedict Mathurin now has 104 points in his first five career games.

He's the first Pacers player to score 100+ points in their first five career games in franchise history. |access-date=November 2, 2022}} On October 29, Mathurin set a career high with 32 points on 6–of–9 three-point shooting and five rebounds in a 125–116 win over the [[2022–23 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Mathurin helps Pacers top Nets 125-116 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401468238 |website=ESPN |access-date=October 30, 2022 |date=October 29, 2022}} On November 9, Mathurin recorded 30 points on 10–of–17 shooting from the field and 6–of–9 shooting from three in a loss to the [[2022–23 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web |title=Bennedict Mathurin (30 Points) Highlights Vs. Denver Nuggets |url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/bennedict-mathurin-30-points-highlights-vs-denver-nuggets |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 9, 2022 |date=October 29, 2022}} On December 1, Mathurin was named [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] [[NBA Rookie of the Month Award|Rookie of the Month]], averaging 19.2 points, 4 rebounds, on 40.3% three-point shooting.{{cite web |title=Jalen Williams, Bennedict Mathurin named Kia Rookies of the Month |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-rookies-of-the-month-oct-nov-2022-23 |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 2, 2022 |date=December 1, 2022}} On January 31, 2023, Mathurin was named a 2023 [[NBA Rising Star]] alongside standout rookie teammate [[Andrew Nembhard]].{{cite web |last=Frank |first=Evan |date=2023-01-23 |title=Pacers' Bennedict Mathurin, Andrew Nembhard named NBA Rising Stars for All-Star Weekend |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2023/01/31/pacers-bennedict-mathurin-andrew-nembhard-named-nba-rising-stars/69858891007/ |access-date=2023-01-23 |website=IndyStar.com}} On February 13, after scoring 21 points against the [[2022–23 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]], Mathurin became the fastest Pacer rookie since [[Chuck Person]] in the [[1986–87 Indiana Pacers season|1986–87 season]] to reach 1,000 career points.{{cite web |author=Indiana Pacers |date=February 13, 2023 |title=Bennedict Mathurin is the fastest Pacers rookie since Chuck Person (1986-87) to reach 1,000 career points. |url=https://twitter.com/Pacers/status/1625290283758788613 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=Twitter}} With the Pacers dropping out of [[2023 NBA playoffs|playoff]] contention, Mathurin became a starter over the last 10 games of his rookie season.{{cite web |last=East |first=Tony |date=March 21, 2023 |title=Bennedict Mathurin returns for Indiana Pacers with 18 point outing against Charlotte Hornets |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/news/bennedict-mathurin-returns-indiana-pacers-18-point-outing-charlotte-hornets |access-date=March 21, 2023 |website=SportsIllustrated.com}}{{cite web |date=March 24, 2023 |title=Pacers' Buddy Hield: Moves to bench role Friday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-buddy-hield-moves-to-bench-role-friday |access-date=March 24, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com}} On March 28, as a starter against the [[2022–23 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]], Mathurin recorded 29 points and a career-high 9 rebounds, while passing teammate [[Chris Duarte (basketball)|Chris Duarte]] for most three-pointers made as a rookie in Pacers franchise history.{{cite web |date=March 28, 2023 |title=Pacers' Bennedict Mathurin: Nears double-double in defeat |date=March 28, 2023}} At the [[2022–23 Indiana Pacers season|2022–23]] season's end, he finished fourth in the 2023 [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]] voting{{cite web |title=2023 NBA Rookie of the Year Voting |website=[[Associated Press News]] |date=25 April 2023 |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-35b9793aef42d37b116bf3e90a1f8e36}} and earned [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All–Rookie First Team]] honors.{{cite web |title=2022-23 Kia NBA All-Rookie teams |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-23-all-rookie-teams-announced}} ====2023–24 season: Season–ending shoulder injury==== On November 8, 2023, Mathurin recorded 22 points, 9 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 steals, along with 4 threes made in a win against the [[Utah Jazz]]. On November 9, the next day, he scored 26 points to go along with a 11 rebounds, a steal, and a block in a win against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. On February 17, 2024, Mathurin was named MVP of the [[2024 NBA All-Star Game|2024]] [[NBA Rising Stars Challenge]] (as part of [[NBA All-Star weekend|NBA All–Star Weekend]]), which was played in [[Indianapolis]] at [[Gainbridge Fieldhouse]]. He notably scored 22 total points in the Rising Stars tournament and helped lead Team [[Jalen Rose|Jalen]] to a Rising Stars championship.{{cite web | last=Dopirak | first=Dustin | title=NBA-All-Star: Bennedict Mathurin calls his shot, wins Rising Stars MVP | website=IndyStar | date=2024-02-17 | url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2024/02/17/bennedict-mathurin-calls-his-shot-wins-rising-stars-mvp/72638581007/ | access-date=2025-12-11}} On March 9, Mathurin was diagnosed with a torn labrum in his right shoulder, an injury which required surgery. He missed the remainder of the [[2023–24 Indiana Pacers season|2023–24 season]].{{cite web |title=Pacers' Bennedict Mathurin to have season-ending shoulder surgery |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=https://www.nba.com/news/pacers-bennedict-mathurin-season-ending-shoulder-surgery|date=2024-03-09|access-date=2024-03-10}} Despite Mathurin's injury the Pacers made it to the [[NBA conference finals|Eastern Conference Finals]]. ====2024–25 season: NBA Finals appearance==== On November 10, 2024, Mathurin put up a career-high 38 points with 7-of-8 three-pointers made in a 132–121 win over the [[New York Knicks]]. He and [[Tyrese Haliburton]] became the second duo to each score at least 35 points in a game in Pacers franchise history,{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pacers-news-tyrese-haliburton-bennedict-mathurin-history-knicks-takedown|title=Tyrese Haliburton, Bennedict Mathurin make Pacers history in Knicks takedown|website=ClutchPoints|last=Villas|first=Rexwell|date=November 10, 2024|access-date=November 10, 2024}} after [[Jalen Rose]] and [[Reggie Miller]] during the [[2000 NBA playoffs|2000 NBA Eastern Conference Semifinals]] against the [[1999–2000 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200005060IND.html|title=2000 Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals|website=Basketball Reference|date=May 6, 2000|access-date=May 12, 2025}} On March 20, 2025, Mathurin scored 28 points and collected a career-high 16 rebounds in an overtime win over the [[2024–25 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]]. On May 29, he recorded 23 points and 9 rebounds, both team-highs, on 6-10 shooting and 9-9 free throws, in a game-five loss to the [[2024–25 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]] in the [[NBA conference finals|Eastern Conference Finals]]. The Pacers eventually won the series, advancing to the [[2025 NBA Finals]]. On June 11, Mathurin scored a playoff career-high 27 points in only 22 minutes off the bench in a 116–107 Game 3 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] to help the Pacers take a 2–1 series lead.{{cite web|last=Collier|first=Jamal|title=Bennedict Mathurin, Pacers top Thunder in NBA Finals Game 3|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45496551/bennedict-mathurin-pacers-top-thunder-nba-finals-game-3|website=ESPN|date=June 11, 2025|access-date=June 11, 2025}} ====2025–26 season==== Mathurin made 28 appearances (including 24 starts) for the Pacers during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 17.8 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Bennedict Mathurin 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683634/bennedict-mathurin|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} === Los Angeles Clippers (2026) === On February 5, 2026, Brown]].{{Cite web |title=CLIPPERS ACQUIRE MATHURIN, JACKSON AND TWO FIRST-ROUND PICKS FROM INDIANA web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/los-angeles-clippers/clippers-news-bennedict-mathurin-makes-franchise-history-vs-nuggets|title=Clippers’ Bennedict Mathurin makes franchise history with nuclear
